from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

        # Already visualizing vectors, just highlighting

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lines = [
            "Cramer's Rule relates areas to variables.",
            "Swap columns with the target vector.",
            "Substituted areas scale with the unknown weight.",
            "Ratio of these areas yields the variable.",
            "This reveals the geometry behind the rule."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Geometric Substitution (Cramer's Insight)", lines)
        
        # Define vectors
        v1 = np.array([1, 0.5, 0])
        v2 = np.array([0.2, 1, 0])
        b = np.array([0.7, 1.2, 0])

        # Create Parallelogram
        def get_parallelogram(a, b, color):
            return Polygon(ORIGIN, a, a+b, b, color=color, fill_opacity=0.3)

        para_orig = get_parallelogram(v1, v2, BLUE)
        para_sub = get_parallelogram(b, v2, ORANGE)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(para_orig))
        self.lecture[0].set_color(BLUE)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===

        self.play(TransformFromCopy(para_orig, para_sub))
        self.place_at_grid(para_sub, 'C3')

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===

        self.setup_layout("Visual Proof: Area Scaling", [

        area_tracker = ValueTracker(1.0)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(BLUE))
        self.play(Create(para1), Create(para2), Write(label1), Write(label2))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        
        para2.add_updater(lambda m: m.set_points(
            Polygon(ORIGIN, RIGHT*2, RIGHT*2+UP*area_tracker.get_value()*2, UP*area_tracker.get_value()*2, color=YELLOW).get_points()
        ))
        self.play(area_tracker.animate.set_value(2.0), run_time=2)
        self.play(area_tracker.animate.set_value(0.5), run_time=2)

        self.play(area_tracker.animate.set_value(1.0))

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Summary and Geometric Constraint", [
            "Singular systems have a zero determinant.", 
            "Columns collapse into a single line.", 
            "The target vector becomes unreachable."
        ])
        
        # Create vectors and area
        v1 = Vector([1.5, 0.5], color=RED)
        v2 = Vector([3.0, 1.0], color=RED)
        parallelogram = Polygon(ORIGIN, v1.get_end(), v1.get_end() + v2.get_end(), v2.get_end(), 
                               fill_opacity=0.3, fill_color=YELLOW, stroke_color=YELLOW)
        
        target_b = Dot(point=self.grid["D5"], color=BLUE)
        b_label = Text("b", font_size=20, color=BLUE).next_to(target_b, RIGHT)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(v1), FadeIn(v2), FadeIn(parallelogram))
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(v2.animate.put_start_and_end_on(ORIGIN, [1.5, 0.5, 0]),
                  parallelogram.animate.become(Line(ORIGIN, [1.5, 0.5, 0], color=YELLOW)))
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(target_b), Write(b_label))
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.wait(2)

sections.title: Prerequisites: Vectors as Area Operators
sections.content: Briefly recall that a 2x2 determinant represents the signed area of a parallelogram formed by two column vectors. If the determinant is zero, the vectors are collinear (area collapses).
sections.example: Visualizing two vectors, v1=(2,1) and v2=(1,2), forming a parallelogram in the Cartesian plane.

sections.title: The Linear System as a Geometric Puzzle
sections.content: Represent the system Ax = b as a vector equation: x1(column1) + x2(column2) = b. Explain that we are trying to find the 'weights' (x1, x2) that scale these columns to reach target vector b.
sections.example: An archer (the vector b) stands at (5, 5). Two elastic bands (column vectors) must be stretched by factors x1 and x2 to hit the bullseye.

sections.title: Geometric Substitution (Cramer's Insight)
sections.content: Introduce Cramer’s Rule: x1 = det(A1)/det(A) and x2 = det(A2)/det(A). Explain that substituting the target vector b into the first column creates a new parallelogram whose area is scaled by x1.
sections.example: Animation showing the original parallelogram defined by (col1, col2) being swapped for (b, col2) to reveal the area ratio.

sections.title: Visual Proof: Area Scaling
sections.content: Demonstrate that the ratio of the area of the 'substituted' parallelogram to the original parallelogram is exactly the value of the unknown variable. This provides the 'Aha!' moment.
sections.example: A split-screen animation: Left side shows the variable x1 changing; right side shows the area of the modified parallelogram expanding and contracting in perfect synchronization.

sections.title: Summary and Geometric Constraint
sections.content: Conclude by noting that if det(A)=0, the column vectors are parallel (the area is zero), making division impossible—this is the geometric reason why systems with no unique solutions fail Cramer's Rule.
sections.example: The 'Crushed Parallelogram': Two column vectors collapsing into a single line, rendering the target vector b unreachable unless it lies on that same line.
